description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, representing ACC (%), spans from 60 to 80. The Base method, depicted by a black line with circle markers, starts at approximately 61% and increases steadily to about 66%. The MEND method, shown as a brown line with diamond markers, begins at around 66% and rises to approximately 74%. The FT method, represented by a blue line with triangle markers, starts near 63% and ends at about 68%. The MEMIT method, indicated by a purple line with star markers, begins at roughly 66% and climbs to approximately 72%. The IKE method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at about 65% and increases to around 70%. The ROME method, depicted by a green line with square markers, begins at approximately 72% and remains relatively flat, stabilizing near 78% across the entire range of the x-axis.
